channel.title: Said & Checked: Missouri — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day from or about Missouri, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Missouri, 2026-11-22: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Josh Hawley)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Josh Hawley, U.S. Senator: “Congress should pass my bipartisan bill to cap these rates and deliver relief right away,” Unsettled. Congress's bill records show Hawley sponsored S. 2760 in the 118th Congress, a credit card rate cap with no cosponsors. In the 119th Congress he is a cosponsor, added the day it was introduced (Feb. 4, 2025), of S. 381, the 10 Percent Credit Card Interest Rate Cap Act sponsored by Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), whose other cosponsors are Democrats Merkley and Gillibrand. Whether "my bipartisan bill" fits a bill he cosponsors rather than sponsors is a question of wording the records do not settle.

item.title: Said & Checked, Missouri, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Eric Schmitt)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Eric Schmitt, U.S. Senator from Missouri: “Since the authorization and the Working Families Tax Cut, a little over a year ago, 70 percent of copper wire has been replaced with fiber, nearly 470 radios converted to modernized systems, new electronic flight strips installed in 25 control…” Unsettled. The FAA's Nov. 5, 2026 release reports 69% of copper wiring replaced, electronic flight strips in 26 towers and 226 IP voice switches, consistent with the statement. No FAA figure for 'nearly 470 radios' was found; GAO reports radio-site work at 17% of 1,581 planned sites (about 269) as of May 2026, so the radio figure is neither confirmed nor ruled out.
  • Eric Schmitt, U.S. Senator from Missouri: “this would authorize the National Park Service's ability to enter into a defined agreement with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation to manage, market, and execute private events at Gateway Arch National Park.” Unsettled. Section 3(a) of H.R. 5254 (Senate-reported text) lets the Interior Secretary enter a one-time agreement of up to five years with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation 'to host private events at the Park'; AskAmerica's CRS bill summary matches. The text says 'host' and does not mention managing or marketing events, so whether it covers those is a reading.
